children: In the six months to September end, pre-tax losses widened to £121.2m from £71.1m in the same period a year earlier. Net rental income fell 10.9% to £52.3m following disposals, with underlying net rental income 7.3% lower at £51.8m.

Property valuation declined 6.6% to £1.98bn and Workspace said it was deferring a decision on its interim dividend until the full-year results, when it expects to have greater visibility on disposals and the cost of refinancing.
Occupancy was 79.2%, versus 79.8% at the end of March and 78.3% in the same period a year earlier.

Chief executive Charlie Green said: "Occupancy and rents remained stable despite quieter customer activity in the second quarter. Trading is in line with our expectations, while portfolio valuations reflect the upward pressure on property yields amid increased volatility in bond markets.

"The board remains focused on disciplined capital allocation, including continuing to invest in the existing portfolio to drive rental growth. In light of the current pace of disposals and the importance of supporting the group’s investment-grade rating, it has deferred a decision on the interim dividend until the full-year results, when it expects to have greater visibility on disposals and the cost of refinancing.

"We are in a period of transition as we reshape our offer and transform the business. The changes we are making to Workspace will take time to fully deliver. With encouraging early progress, we are increasingly confident in the potential of the business to generate sustainable earnings growth and long-term shareholder value."
At 0945 GMT, the shares were down 5.7% at 319.20p.
